candidate.title: Support promotional discount codes in cart pricing
candidate.problem_statement: Marketing teams need the ability to apply discount codes during checkout to drive promotions. Currently, `compute_totals` only accounts for subtotal, tax, and shipping, without supporting item-level or order-level discounts. Adding a coupon code mechanism allows carts to calculate valid discount deductions and adjust final totals.
requirements: Create a `DiscountCoupon` dataclass in `shopcart.pricing` with fields `code: str`, `discount_percent: Decimal = Decimal('0')`, `fixed_amount: Decimal = Decimal('0')`, and `min_subtotal: Decimal = Decimal('0')`.
Add an optional `coupon: DiscountCoupon | None = None` parameter to `compute_totals(cart: Cart, policy: PricingPolicy | None = None, coupon: DiscountCoupon | None = None) -> Totals`.
Add a `discount: Decimal` field to `Totals` (default `Decimal('0.00')`). The final `total` property in `Totals` must equal `subtotal - discount + tax + shipping`.
If a coupon is provided but `cart.subtotal()` is strictly less than `coupon.min_subtotal`, raise `PricingError` (a subclass of `Exception`).

Discount amount is calculated as `percent_of(cart.subtotal(), coupon.discount_percent) + to_money(coupon.fixed_amount)`. The calculated discount cannot exceed `cart.subtotal()`; if it exceeds `cart.subtotal()`, clamp `discount` to `cart.subtotal()`.

Tax must be calculated on the discounted subtotal (`cart.subtotal() - discount`), using the existing tax policy logic distributed proportionally across lines, or applying the effective rate: compute tax on each line's proportional share after discount (rounded to `CENT`). If discount equals subtotal, tax is `Decimal('0.00')`.
acceptance_criteria: Calling `compute_totals(cart, coupon=coupon)` with `min_subtotal` greater than `cart.subtotal()` raises `PricingError`.
Valid percent discount reduces `subtotal` by `percent_of(cart.subtotal(), coupon.discount_percent)` and records it in `Totals.discount`.
A fixed-amount coupon exceeding the subtotal clamps `Totals.discount` to `cart.subtotal()` and does not result in a negative total.
`Totals.total` precisely matches `subtotal - discount + tax + shipping`.
candidate.existing_behaviour: Totals only tracks subtotal, tax, shipping, and total (which is subtotal + tax + shipping). PricingPolicy has no discount concept.
edge_cases: Subtotal exactly equals min_subtotal: coupon is valid and applied.
Discount is larger than subtotal: discount is clamped to subtotal, resulting in $0.00 subtotal-after-discount and $0.00 tax.
Both discount_percent and fixed_amount are specified: their sum is discounted up to subtotal.

contract.name: PricingError
contract.behaviour: Raised when pricing operations fail, such as when a coupon does not meet the minimum subtotal requirement.

contract.name: DiscountCoupon
contract.signature:
class DiscountCoupon:
    code: str
    discount_percent: Decimal = Decimal('0')
    fixed_amount: Decimal = Decimal('0')
    min_subtotal: Decimal = Decimal('0')
contract.behaviour: Represents a promotional discount coupon with percentage and/or fixed amount savings and an optional minimum subtotal threshold.

candidate.title: Add order refund and return lifecycle states
candidate.problem_statement: Customer support agents currently cannot process returns or refunds on fulfilled orders. The order state machine only transitions up to `SHIPPED` or `CANCELLED`. Adding return and refund transitions allows the platform to properly track returned merchandise and restock inventory.
requirements: Add `REFUNDED` and `RETURNED` members to `OrderStatus` enum in `shopcart.orders`.

Update `ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS` to allow: `OrderStatus.PAID -> {OrderStatus.SHIPPED, OrderStatus.REFUNDED}`, `OrderStatus.SHIPPED -> {OrderStatus.RETURNED}`, and `OrderStatus.RETURNED -> {OrderStatus.REFUNDED}`.
Add `refund(self)` method to `Order`. If status is `PAID` or `RETURNED`, transition to `REFUNDED`. Calling `refund()` from any other status raises `OrderError`.

Add `return_items(self, inventory: Inventory)` method to `Order`. If status is `SHIPPED`, transition to `RETURNED` and call `inventory.restock(item.sku, item.quantity)` for each item in the order. Calling `return_items` from any status other than `SHIPPED` raises `OrderError`.
acceptance_criteria: Invoking `order.return_items(inventory)` on a `SHIPPED` order changes status to `RETURNED` and increments inventory available stock by the quantities of items in the order.
Invoking `order.refund()` on a `RETURNED` order transitions status to `REFUNDED`.
Invoking `order.refund()` on a `PAID` order (before shipping) transitions status to `REFUNDED` without restocking (since stock is cancelled/handled separately).
Attempting `order.return_items(inventory)` on a `PENDING` or `PAID` order raises `OrderError`.
candidate.existing_behaviour: OrderStatus has PENDING, PAID, SHIPPED, CANCELLED. PAID can only transition to SHIPPED. SHIPPED is a terminal state with no outbound transitions.
edge_cases: Attempting to refund an already REFUNDED order raises OrderError.
Attempting to return items on a CANCELLED order raises OrderError.
Calling return_items with multiple distinct SKUs restocks all line items in the inventory.

contract.name: Order.refund
contract.behaviour: Transitions an order in PAID or RETURNED state to REFUNDED, or raises OrderError if invalid.

contract.name: Order.return_items
contract.behaviour: Transitions an order in SHIPPED state to RETURNED and restocks all order line items back into inventory.

candidate.title: Add inventory valuation and stock report aggregation
candidate.problem_statement: Warehouse and operations managers need visibility into total inventory levels, available versus reserved quantities, and the total monetary value of on-hand inventory. Currently, inventory tracking only exposes individual SKU lookups without aggregate reporting or catalog price cross-referencing.
requirements: Create an `InventoryReport` dataclass in `shopcart.inventory` with fields: `total_on_hand: int`, `total_reserved: int`, `total_available: int`, `total_valuation: Decimal`, and `sku_breakdown: dict[str, dict[str, int | Decimal]]`.
Implement `generate_inventory_report(inventory: Inventory, catalog: Catalog) -> InventoryReport` in `shopcart.inventory`.

For each SKU tracked in `inventory`, `sku_breakdown[sku]` must contain keys: `'on_hand'` (int), `'reserved'` (int), `'available'` (int), and `'valuation'` (Decimal, equal to `on_hand * product.price` from `catalog`).
If a SKU in inventory is not found in `catalog`, default its unit price to `Decimal('0.00')` for valuation calculations.

`total_on_hand` is the sum of all `on_hand` quantities. `total_reserved` is the sum of all `reserved` quantities. `total_available` is the sum of all `available` quantities (`on_hand - reserved`). `total_valuation` is the sum of all SKU valuations, rounded to `CENT`.
acceptance_criteria: `generate_inventory_report` returns an `InventoryReport` with accurate totals across all tracked items.
`sku_breakdown` contains correct on-hand, reserved, available, and valuation metrics for each SKU.
Unlisted SKUs in inventory have valuation `Decimal('0.00')` without raising key errors.
Empty inventory returns zeroed totals and an empty breakdown dictionary.
candidate.existing_behaviour: Inventory maintains internal on_hand and reserved dicts, but only exposes `available(sku: str) -> int`. There is no batch query or monetary valuation.
edge_cases: Inventory has no items restocked: returns report with all totals 0 and empty dictionary.
SKU has stock reserved: available is on_hand - reserved, and valuation is based on total on_hand.
Catalog lookup for SKU raises KeyError: gracefully handled by valuing SKU at 0.00.

contract.name: InventoryReport
contract.signature:
class InventoryReport:
    total_on_hand: int
    total_reserved: int
    total_available: int
    total_valuation: Decimal
    sku_breakdown: dict[str, dict[str, int | Decimal]]
contract.behaviour: Represents an aggregated inventory status and valuation report.

contract.name: generate_inventory_report
contract.signature: def generate_inventory_report(inventory: Inventory, catalog: Catalog) -> InventoryReport
contract.behaviour: Calculates aggregate inventory quantities and catalog-based monetary valuation across all tracked inventory SKUs.

candidate.title: Configurable tiered shipping policy based on cart weight
candidate.problem_statement: Logistics managers need shipping costs to be computed dynamically based on package weight tiers rather than just a flat rate and price threshold. Currently `PricingPolicy` only calculates shipping using a flat `shipping_rate` and `free_shipping_threshold` on cart subtotal.
requirements: Add an optional `weight: Decimal = Decimal('0.0')` field (in kilograms/pounds) to `Product` in `shopcart.catalog`.

Create a `WeightTierShippingPolicy` in `shopcart.pricing` with `tiers: list[tuple[Decimal, Decimal]]` (list of `(max_weight, shipping_fee)` pairs sorted ascending by `max_weight`), and `fallback_rate_per_unit_weight: Decimal = Decimal('2.00')`.
Implement `compute_cart_weight(cart: Cart) -> Decimal` in `shopcart.pricing` that calculates `sum(item.product.weight * item.quantity for item in cart.lines())`.
Implement `calculate_shipping_by_weight(cart: Cart, policy: WeightTierShippingPolicy) -> Decimal` in `shopcart.pricing`.

Shipping rule: If cart is empty, shipping is `Decimal('0.00')`. Otherwise, find the first tier where `total_weight <= max_weight` and return `to_money(tier_shipping_fee)`. If total weight exceeds all tiers, shipping is `highest_tier_fee + (total_weight - max_tier_weight) * fallback_rate_per_unit_weight` rounded to `CENT`.
acceptance_criteria: Empty cart has shipping cost `Decimal('0.00')`.
Cart with weight falling into the first tier returns the first tier's fee.
Cart with weight matching tier boundary exactly selects that tier.
Cart exceeding the highest tier weight applies the fallback rate per excess unit weight added to the highest tier fee.
candidate.existing_behaviour: PricingPolicy only checks if subtotal >= free_shipping_threshold to set shipping to 0, otherwise charges flat shipping_rate. Product has no weight attribute.
edge_cases: Product created without specifying weight defaults to Decimal('0.0').
Cart with 0.0 total weight matches tier 0 if max_weight >= 0, or lowest tier.
WeightTierShippingPolicy with empty tiers raises ValueError when evaluated against non-empty cart.

contract.name: WeightTierShippingPolicy
contract.behaviour: Configurable tiered weight policy mapping maximum weight limits to shipping rates.

contract.name: compute_cart_weight
contract.behaviour: Sums the total weight of all line items in the cart.

contract.name: calculate_shipping_by_weight
contract.signature: def calculate_shipping_by_weight(cart: Cart, policy: WeightTierShippingPolicy) -> Decimal
contract.behaviour: Calculates total shipping cost for a cart using weight tiers and fallback rates.

candidate.title: Add cart merge and transfer capabilities
candidate.problem_statement: Users who browse anonymously and then log in need their guest cart merged into their account cart without losing items. Currently, `Cart` has no method to absorb or transfer items from another cart, requiring manual per-item iteration and re-validation.
requirements: Implement `merge(self, other: Cart) -> None` on `Cart` in `shopcart.cart`.
When `cart_a.merge(cart_b)` is called, each item in `cart_b.lines()` is added to `cart_a` using `add_item` logic.
If adding items from `other` would cause any item in `cart_a` to exceed `MAX_QUANTITY_PER_LINE`, do not modify `cart_a` (atomic operation) and raise `CartError`.

After successfully merging into `cart_a`, the caller may choose whether `other` is cleared: provide parameter `clear_source: bool = False`. If `True`, `other.clear()` is called after successful merge.

If `cart_a` and `cart_b` reference different catalogs, allow the merge if all items in `cart_b` exist in `cart_a.catalog`; if any SKU in `cart_b` does not exist in `cart_a.catalog`, raise `CartError` without modifying either cart.
acceptance_criteria: `cart_a.merge(cart_b)` combines quantities for identical SKUs and appends new SKUs to `cart_a`.
If merging causes an item quantity to exceed 99, `CartError` is raised and `cart_a` is unchanged.
If `clear_source=True`, `cart_b.is_empty()` is `True` after merge.
If merge fails due to capacity limit or missing catalog SKU, neither `cart_a` nor `cart_b` is modified.
candidate.existing_behaviour: Cart only supports individual add_item, update_quantity, remove_item, and clear operations. There is no bulk or multi-cart operation.
edge_cases: Merging an empty cart into cart_a does nothing and succeeds.
Merging cart_a into itself raises CartError.
Failure halfway through checking line limits rolls back any in-memory state changes.

contract.name: Cart.merge
contract.signature: def merge(self, other: Cart, clear_source: bool = False) -> None
contract.behaviour: Merges all line items from another cart into this cart atomically, optionally clearing the source cart upon success.

candidate.title: Validate cart items availability directly against inventory
candidate.problem_statement: Shoppers often proceed toward checkout only to find order placement fails due to out-of-stock items. A checkout pre-flight check is needed to validate that all items in a cart are currently available in inventory and to return a detailed availability summary before attempting order creation.
requirements: Create an `AvailabilityIssue` dataclass in `shopcart.cart` with fields `sku: str`, `requested: int`, and `available: int`.
Create a `CartValidationResult` dataclass in `shopcart.cart` with fields `is_valid: bool` and `issues: list[AvailabilityIssue]`.
Implement `validate_cart_availability(cart: Cart, inventory: Inventory) -> CartValidationResult` in `shopcart.cart`.
For each `LineItem` in `cart.lines()`: check `inventory.available(sku)`. If `requested > available`, append an `AvailabilityIssue(sku=item.sku, requested=item.quantity, available=avail)` to issues.
Issues must be ordered alphabetically by `sku`. `is_valid` is `True` if and only if `len(issues) == 0`.
acceptance_criteria: If all cart items have `inventory.available(sku) >= quantity`, returns `CartValidationResult(is_valid=True, issues=[])`.
If one or more items exceed available stock, returns `is_valid=False` with all affected items in `issues` sorted by SKU.
Empty cart returns `CartValidationResult(is_valid=True, issues=[])`.
Function does not mutate cart contents or inventory reservations.
candidate.existing_behaviour: Cart has no reference to Inventory. Inventory reservations only happen during Order.place, which throws InventoryError if stock is insufficient.
edge_cases: Item in cart has 0 available inventory: issue has available=0.
Cart has multiple items where some are valid and some are short: only short items are in issues.
Does not modify inventory or reserve any stock.
